title: DUSRM 0.2 Pilot — FireBot Cyber-Physical Rescue Robot
summary: WP5 profile-reconciliation pilot. Documentation-level architecture description; not a conformance approval.

systemOfInterest.name: FireBot integrated firefighting and human-rescue robot
systemOfInterest.description: Intended integrated robot system described using repository documentation; the current verified scope remains software-first and simulated, with physical implementation not established.

context.purpose: Represent FireBot's software, simulation, intended physical platform, subsystem contracts and safety-policy requirements without confusing design intent with physical implementation.
context.scope: FireBot system architecture, software dashboard/simulation, planned physical platform, proposed subsystem integrations and people-first mission outcomes.

boundary.notes: Boundary selected for the profile pilot; use explicit external participants and planned realization states.

environment.name: Human operator
environment.description: External human operator and emergency authority.

environment.name: Fireground environment
environment.description: Physical fireground and rescue environment; no real-world performance is demonstrated by current simulations.

environment.name: Dashboard host computer
environment.description: External host for software presentation and simulation.

assumptions: FireBot CURRENT_STATE snapshot is dated 2026-10-11 and reports no physical sensors, motors, pump, batteries, cooling system or microphone connected.
Hosted deployment and full Node.js test execution are recorded as requiring verification in the inspected snapshot.
All model-level safety requirements remain design assertions, not physical safety evidence.

org.dmj.dusrm.profile.cps-robot.rule: Never treat simulated or planned telemetry as a measured physical observation; keep local safety authority independent of remote coordination.

elements.name: FireBot dashboard
elements.description: Software dashboard prototype using simulated state.

elements.name: FireBot simulation engine
elements.description: Software simulation for route and scenario progression; not a physics-validated robot model.

elements.name: Simulated power and thermal policy
elements.description: Synthetic thermal zones and simulated power-management behavior; no real sensor measurement or battery controller.

elements.name: Physical robot platform
elements.description: Chassis, motors, batteries, cameras, thermal sensors and pump are intended hardware; none are connected in the inspected state snapshot.

elements.name: Vision subsystem

elements.name: Local safety controller
elements.description: Independent physical safety path is a design requirement, not an implemented controller.

responsibilities.description: Provide human-rescue-first mission support and firefighting capabilities.

realizations.rationale: The repository describes an obstacle-aware software simulation; full Node test/deployment verification remains pending.
Simulation state is represented in software.
Deterministic A* route planning and rule-based simulation are repository-reported.
Dashboard code exists but the hosted bundle still requires verification.
Simulation-only capabilities are represented in the software prototype.

layerApplicability.rationale: Physical platform belongs to the intended full system boundary, but its realization is planned.
Power and compute resource policy is represented in simulation/planning; physical values remain unselected.
Simulation progression is in progress; physical control and local safety are planned.
Robot, mission, detection and power state contracts are modeled; physical state is not established.
Route planning is simulated; real perception and SLAM remain unverified.
Dashboard and subsystem contracts exist; live networking is not established.
Dashboard and simulation capabilities are in progress; physical robot services are not validated.
People-first rescue and firefighting remain intended mission outcomes.

requirements.statement: Mission policy should prioritize unresolved people before fire objectives, subject to safety and operator authority.
acceptanceCriteria: People-first ordering is represented in deterministic scenarios
Low-confidence and stale detections are not promoted to confirmed findings

requirements.statement: Emergency stop and time-sensitive local safety control shall remain independent of host software and network availability.
acceptanceCriteria: Local controller/hardware path operates without dashboard, broker or network
Remote messages cannot silently clear emergency stop

constraints.statement: Remote APIs, network transport, dashboard and mission orchestration are not authoritative for local emergency-stop or immediate actuator safety.
Synthetic simulation values must not be represented as measured physical telemetry.

invariants.statement: In the intended local safety model, emergency stop dominates autonomous command requests and requires an explicit local reset sequence.
assumptions: Design-model requirement only; no physical safety verification is implied.
invariants.method: Repository-documentation mapping; not a safety proof.

assertions.statement: The current recorded FireBot baseline is a software-first dashboard/simulation prototype, not a physically connected robot.
Physical sensors, motors, pump, batteries and cooling remain planned/unconnected in the inspected snapshot.

evidence.description: FireBot current-state snapshot states software-first prototype status and explicitly lists unconnected physical hardware and unverified deployments/tests.
limitations: Snapshot is dated 2026-10-11; it is not a live deployment or test result.

evidence.description: FireBot architecture overview and people-first project intent.
limitations: Architecture describes intended behavior; physical realization is not established.

evidence.description: FireBot status document distinguishes code-present, simulation, planned and unverified work; Node/browser verification still pending in the snapshot.
FireBot interface contracts and simulation status fields.
limitations: Message contracts do not establish live physical subsystem connectivity.

evidence.description: DMJ Systems integration plan requires local safety independence and labels technology integration as proposed/documentation-only.
limitations: Proposed architecture only; no live adapter or safety controller is claimed.

evidence.description: Technology integration specification states candidate projects are proposed and not an implementation baseline.
